function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure! Here are some great options for ordering a cake, whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty bakery, or a nationwide service that can deliver right to your door.

---

## 1. Local Bakeries & Specialty Shops  
*(If you have a city or zip code handy, I can narrow it down further.)*

| Type | What to Look For | Why It’s Great |
|------|------------------|----------------|
| **Independent Artisan Bakeries** | Hand‑crafted, seasonal flavors, often use local ingredients. | Unique taste, support local business. |
| **Café‑Bakery Chains** (e.g., **Starbucks Reserve**, **Café Nero**) | Consistent quality, easy online ordering. | Reliable, quick delivery. |
| **Specialty Cake Shops** (e.g., **Cake Boss**, **The Cake Shop**) | Custom designs, themed cakes. | Perfect for birthdays, weddings. |
| **Farm‑to‑Table Bakeries** | Organic, locally sourced ingredients. | Health‑conscious, eco‑friendly. |

### How to Find Them
- **Google Maps**: Search “cake shop near me” or “custom cake bakery + city”.
- **Yelp**: Look for high‑rated bakeries with recent reviews.
- **Local Food Blogs**: Often feature hidden gems.

---

## 2. National & Online Cake Delivery Services  

| Service | Highlights | Typical Delivery Time |
|---------|------------|-----------------------|
| **Goldbelly** | Curated selection from iconic U.S. bakeries (e.g., Magnolia Bakery, Baked by Melissa). | 1–3 days (depends on destination). |
| **BakeShare** | Community‑based platform; local bakers ship to you. | 1–5 days. |
| **Etsy** | Handmade custom cakes from independent artisans worldwide. | 1–7 days (check seller’s shipping policy). |
| **Amazon Fresh** | Some regions offer cake delivery from local bakeries. | Same‑day or next‑day. |
| **Instacart** | Partner with local grocery stores that carry pre‑made cakes. | Same‑day delivery. |

---

## 3. Specialty & Theme‑Specific Options  

| Theme | Where to Order | Why It Works |
|-------|----------------|--------------|
| **Wedding Cakes** | **Cake Boss**, **The Cake Shop**, or local wedding planners. | Professional design, large sizes. |
| **Birthday Cakes** | **Baked by Melissa**, **Chocoville**, or local bakeries. | Fun shapes, custom messages. |
| **Diet‑Specific (Gluten‑Free, Vegan)** | **Gluten‑Free Bakery**, **Vegan Cake Co.**, or **Goldbelly**’s specialty section. | Meets dietary needs. |
| **Holiday & Seasonal** | **Goldbelly** (e.g., pumpkin spice, Christmas-themed). | Seasonal flavors, limited editions. |

---

## 4. Tips for Ordering a Cake Online  

1. **Check Delivery Radius** – Many bakeries only deliver within a certain distance.  
2. **Read Reviews** – Look for comments about freshness, packaging, and customer service.  
3. **Ask About Customization** – If you want a specific flavor, design, or message, confirm it’s possible.  
4. **Confirm Delivery Date** – Especially for events, order at least a week in advance.  
5. **Packaging** – Ask if they use insulated boxes or temperature‑controlled shipping for long distances.  
6. **Payment & Cancellation Policy** – Make sure you understand how to pay and what happens if you need to cancel or change the order.

---

## 5. Quick Starter List (U.S. Focus)

| City | Bakery / Service | Contact |
|------|------------------|---------|
| New York | **Magnolia Bakery** (Goldbelly) | https://goldbelly.com/magnolia-bakery |
| Los Angeles | **Baked by Melissa** | https://bakedbymelissa.com |
| Chicago | **The Cake Shop** | https://thecakeshop.com |
| Seattle | **Gluten‑Free Bakery** | https://glutenfreebakery.com |
| Nationwide | **Goldbelly** | https://goldbelly.com |
| Nationwide | **Etsy** (search “custom cake”) | https://etsy.com |

---
